reasoning: I read the core docs, contracts, pipelines, tests and plans of both sets, plus three to four packets per set. That sample included one interface-heavy spine, one split thicken task and one system task in each set. On content the two sets tie. Set B has the deeper RL design: a corridor proof of the core, a ladder from tabular to DQN to CNN, ablations, REINFORCE against PPO, self-play with an opponent pool and cross-play. It also stays faithful to the ground truth (a circular tank and one learning predator), and its golden cases are exact and hand-checkable. Set B's design docs carry stale and process text, though. The brief still says 'Not doing: Designing future environments now' and its success criteria cover only Snake. The architecture keeps 'adopted before M1 is built', 'TC-01–TC-49 don't change' and 'pipeline-design … revisit M1's types'. TC-42 contradicts the gae contract on the length of the values array. M1 packs the whole Snake stage, including ablations, the CNN and the reference, into one 31-task milestone, and its 'S'-sized system task trains the full ladder for real. Set A is leaner and better organised. It splits Snake along a real dependency line (M1 train/evaluate, then M2 replay/refcheck/notes), its spec and roadmap agree, and it has a clean single-entry pipeline per command. But A changes the user's circular tank into a square one and uses 2 predators. Its TC-17 noise tolerance would make the test flaky. Two of its spines build modules that belong to another component (the methods factory and runlog.RunWriter), and evaluate.compare is frozen as a helper. Both sets have packets that leave out needed types. Set A wins narrowly on structure: it is clearer to read, has less superseded text, and its layout and organisation are sounder.

strengths: Snake stage split along a real dependency line (M1 train/evaluate, M2 replay/refcheck/notes)
Precise spec with a clear statistical plan (paired permutation test, Holm correction, every run must beat the rule baseline)
Two-exit check corridor whose answers can be worked out by hand and which defeats a learner biased to one action
Each pipeline is one command with one entry; todo, plan and roadmap agree on what to build next
weaknesses: Square tank where the user asked for a circular one; 2 predators where the user asked for one learning predator
TC-17 tolerance is statistically wrong, so the test would be flaky
Spines build modules owned by another component (methods factory, runlog.RunWriter)
S3 only co-trains the two teams; there is no self-play against past opponents
Packets leave out some needed types

strengths: Rich RL learning design: ladders, ablations, REINFORCE vs PPO, opponent-pool self-play, cross-play tables
Faithful to the user's environments (circular tank, one predator, prey foraging for pellets)
Exact, hand-checkable golden cases (TC-12, TC-29, TC-31, TC-42, TC-43, TC-53)
Careful mapping of Stable-Baselines3 settings so the hand-written agents can be compared fairly with the library
weaknesses: Brief is stale against the spec and ideas docs
Process narration and replan history kept in the architecture and plan
M1 covers the whole Snake stage (31 tasks); the system task trains every rung, ablation and reference for real but is sized S
TC-42 disagrees with the gae contract on the length of the values array
Frozen helper functions exposed as test seams (returns_to_go, gae, clipped_objective)
